lines.en: Mia, did you hear? My cousin decided to quit his job yesterday.
lines.pt: Mia, você soube? O meu primo decidiu largar o emprego ontem.

lines.en: Really? He planned to stay until the summer.
lines.pt: Sério? Ele planejava ficar até o verão.

lines.en: Our manager refused to give him a higher salary, so he decided to leave.
lines.pt: Nosso gerente se recusou a dar um salário maior a ele, então ele decidiu sair.

lines.en: That’s hard. Did he agree to work until the end of the month?
lines.pt: Que difícil. Ele concordou em trabalhar até o fim do mês?

lines.en: Yes, he agreed to train the new person, but he refuses to stay longer.
lines.pt: Sim, concordou em treinar a pessoa nova, mas se recusa a ficar mais.

lines.en: I plan to ask for a raise next week. Maybe I should be careful.
lines.pt: Pretendo pedir um aumento semana que vem. Talvez eu deva ter cuidado.

lines.en: Don’t be afraid. I decided to speak with the manager last month.
lines.pt: Não tenha medo. Decidi falar com o gerente no mês passado.

lines.en: And what happened? Did she agree to help you?
lines.pt: E o que aconteceu? Ela concordou em ajudar você?

lines.en: She agreed to give me two extra days off. I still plan to look for a better offer.
lines.pt: Ela concordou em me dar dois dias de folga. Ainda pretendo procurar uma oferta melhor.

lines.en: Smart. I decided to update my résumé tonight. Can you read it?
lines.pt: Esperta. Decidi atualizar meu currículo hoje à noite. Você pode ler?

lines.en: Of course. I agree to read it tonight if you buy the coffee.
lines.pt: Claro. Concordo em lê-lo hoje à noite se você pagar o café.

facts.big: decide / plan / agree / refuse + to + verb
facts.label: Infinitivo depois de verbos
facts.sub: Depois de decide, plan, agree e refuse, use to + verbo: He decided to quit. I plan to ask. She refused to help. Depois do to, use o verbo na forma base.

facts.label: Decidir
facts.sub: Use decide to + verbo para uma escolha: He decided to quit. I decided to speak with the manager. O passado é decided.

facts.label: Planejar
facts.sub: Use plan to + verbo para algo que você pretende fazer: I plan to ask for a raise. They planned to stay. É um projeto, não uma certeza.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “decidiu sair” e “recusou ajudar”, com infinitivo.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.why: We say He decided to quit.

items.s: Refuse to means you say no to doing something.
Agree to means you say yes to doing something.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We say “He decided quitting.” → Falso (We say He decided to quit.)
Refuse to means you say no to doing something. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Agree to means you say yes to doing something. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A big decision · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a windy Wednesday morning in an office in Chicago. People drink coffee and talk in low voices. Dora hears some news about a coworker. She walks to the desk of her friend Mia. Her cousin decided to quit his job. Everyone in the office wants to know why.

“Mia, did you hear? My cousin decided to quit his job yesterday.” says Dora. “Really? He planned to stay until the summer.” says Mia. “Our manager refused to give him a higher salary, so he decided to leave.” says Dora.
